text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Feb 19 - New Zealand's cricket selectors figuratively toasted themselves after the notable debut test series efforts of 18-year-old spin bowler Daniel Vettori.
The bespectacled teenager played in the second and third tests against England and coped admirably with the task.
At Wellington, as New Zealand tumbled to an innings and 68-run loss, he bowled 34.3 overs and took two for 98 in England's only innings.

In the third test, which England won by four wickets at Lancaster Park yesterday, Vettori took one for 13 in 12 overs in the first innings followed by an exhausting 57 overs in the second innings, taking four for 97.
Those two appearances -- only his third and fourth in first-class cricket -- produced seven wickets in three England innings at 29 runs apiece.
He bowled more overs -- 103.2 -- than any other bowler apart from fast-medium Simon Doull, whose 105 overs were spread over three tests.
Only Doull, with nine wickets, had more success than Vettori.
"We're absolutely delighted," chairman of selectors Ross Dykes said last night.
"I'd be lying if I said we didn't cross our fingers (before picking him).
"But we felt the evidence was such that he could cope with it and he's proved it more than adequately."

Dykes said selecting any new player had an element of risk, but after discussing Vettori's qualities with a variety of people who have spent time with him in his formative cricket years, they were satisfied with what they heard.
"I guess you cross your fingers whenever you pick a new player," he said.
"But we believed that he had the maturity and the mental capability of coping with it and I think in two test matches he's proved that."

Vettori hasn't been named in the 12-strong squad for the first two games in the one-day series against England -- and don't expect his name to appear in the refreshed squad for the last three matches.
Dykes said the selectors want him to remain an attacking spin bowler. One-day cricket could alter that approach.
"We're aware that he's an attacking bowler and we want to preserve him as that," Dykes said.
"We don't want to run the risk of having him play in a one-day game and be forced to become defensive."
Vettori played nine of Northern Districts' 12 Shell Cup one-day games earlier this season, taking five wickets at a cost of 62 runs apiece and conceding just over four runs an over.
Now the national selectors -- Dykes, Rick Pickard and Mike Shrimpton -- will put Vettori on ice until the two test matches against Sri Lanka next month.
The spin bowling in the first two one-dayers against England has been entrusted to veteran offspinner Dipak Patel and slow-medium leg spinner Chris Harris.
